advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or repurpose `test_module_declares_a_positive_git_timeout` — it asserts the internal `_GIT_TIMEOUT` name, not observable behavior, and duplicates the kwarg-inspection tests.
evidence: `timeout = getattr(module, "_GIT_TIMEOUT", None)` / `assert timeout is not None, f"{module_path} declares no _GIT_TIMEOUT"` (test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py:76-77)

The observable bound is independently verified by `test_clone_change_ref_passes_a_timeout_to_every_subprocess_call` (line 85) and `test_workspace_git_passes_a_timeout` (line 169), which assert the `timeout` kwarg on each call — these survive a rename of `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, this test does not.
advisory.finding: test_module_declares_a_positive_git_timeout asserts the existence and value of the private module-level constant `_GIT_TIMEOUT` by name, rather than any observable behavior. A behavior-preserving rename of the constant (its callers updated) breaks this test with no change in observable behavior — a Rule-4 change-detector. The observable bounding behavior is already covered by the tests that inspect the `timeout` kwarg actually passed to git calls.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `_redact` (or the error path) with an empty `gerrit_bot_token` returns the text unchanged, covering the explicitly-fixed `str.replace("", "***")` edge.
evidence: Diff/ticket explicitly call this out: "the old inline code did `str.replace(\"\", \"***\")` on an empty token, which inserts `***` between every character"
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `gerrit_bot_token=""` in tests returned no matches; the test fixture always uses `_TOKEN = "s3cr3t-bot-token"` (test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py:38).
advisory.finding: The empty-token edge fix in `GerritClient._redact` (`if not tok: return out`, guarding against the old `str.replace("", "***")` that inserted `***` between every character) is untested. No test constructs a client with an empty `gerrit_bot_token` and asserts `_redact`/the error path leaves the text unchanged, so a regression reintroducing the empty-token corruption would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test building a client with `gerrit_bot_token=""` and asserting `gc._redact("abc") == "abc"` (no `***` inserted).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct `_git_op` unit test (list and string `cmd`, with and without a leading `-C <dir>`) asserting the extracted subcommand, since the error-message substring assertion cannot distinguish a correct extraction from the `git` fallback.
evidence: `_git_op` walks parts skipping argv[0] and `-C <dir>` to find the subcommand, falling back to `"git"` (gerrit_client.py:58-73)

Error message embeds BOTH `git {_git_op(exc.cmd)} ...` AND `{self._redact(exc.cmd)[:500]}` (gerrit_client.py:392-393), so the full fetch argv — which contains `fetch` — is in the message regardless of `_git_op`'s return
Test assertion `assert "fetch" in message.lower(), ...` (test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py:134) therefore passes even if `_git_op` returned the `"git"` fallback.
advisory.finding: `_git_op`'s subcommand-extraction logic (skipping `git` argv[0] and a leading `-C <dir>` global option) is not directly asserted. The descriptive-error test's `assert "fetch" in message.lower()` cannot verify `_git_op` returned `fetch`, because the redacted `exc.cmd` (the full `git -C ... fetch ...` argv) is also embedded in the message and already contains the substring `fetch`; a `_git_op` regression returning the `"git"` fallback would still pass.
